keyframe_review.note: 1949-1952, 112,409 km2, bbox 9.85-15.01 E, 50.25-54.75 N: the Soviet zone of five states plus East Berlin (the gazetteer finds 3 cells of Berlin inside the shape and none of the FRG shape). Infobox gives 108,333 km2 (no year), ratio 1.04, so the shape is sound. The GDR was established on 7 October 1949 ("On 7 October 1949 the SED established the German Democratic Republic").

1953-1972, 112,473 km2, identical outline to 1949. The page records the 1952 redistricting that abolished the five states ("The five original East German states that had been abolished in the 1952 redistricting were restored"), an internal change; no outer border moved. The Inner German border page: the GDR fortified it from 26 May 1952; the Polish line was recognised in 1950 (Oder-Neisse page).

1973-1975, 113,167 km2 (+0.6 % on the neighbouring shapes, +693 km2, bbox unchanged). No opened page dates a border change in 1973; the Inner German border page says only that a "series of treaties and agreements in the early 1970s" followed the 1967-1989 "modern frontier". Treated as outline noise: the renderer should use the 1953/1976 outline for these three years if it can; the difference is under one H3 cell row.

1976-1989, 112,473 km2, the same outline as 1953-1972. Infobox 108,333 km2, ratio 1.04. No page opened dates any change of the outer border in these years; the Berlin Wall (12/13 August 1961) and the fortified inner German border (1952) did not move the line.

1990, 112,473 km2, the unchanged outline to the accession: "Germany was officially reunited at 00:00 CEST on 3 October 1990". The shape runs to the end of 1990 although the state ended on 3 October; the Federated Republic of Germany row takes the land from 1991.

union.text: East Berlin, the Soviet sector, which the GDR "regarded ... as its capital"

region.text: the five states of the Soviet Occupation Zone (Brandenburg, Mecklenburg, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia) and East Berlin

ledger.note: 1949: the SED establishes the German Democratic Republic in the Soviet zone, with East Berlin as capital. "On 7 October 1949 the SED established the German Democratic Republic"; "the Soviet Occupation Zone (Sowjetische Besatzungszone, SBZ) comprised the five states"; "East Germany regarded East Berlin as its capital".

region.text: the whole GDR, five states and East Berlin

ledger.note: 1990: the five East German states join the Federal Republic. "Germany was officially reunited at 00:00 CEST on 3 October 1990"; the five Lander "Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony..." held their first elections on 14 October 1990; "East Berlin, the capital of East Germany, reunited with West Berlin"; the accession was declared by the Volkskammer on 23 August 1990 under Article 23 of the Basic Law.

1990: the GDR is absorbed into the Federal Republic, which "continued to exist under the same legal personality that was founded in May 1949" (Cliopatria draws the enlarged state as the Federated Republic of Germany from 1991).
1990: the GDR ceases to exist on 3 October. "The GDR ceased to exist when its five states" joined the Federal Republic; infobox "Reunification: 3 October 1990".

wars.name: Berlin Crisis of 1961
wars.outcome: No territory changed hands: "the GDR closed the inner German border" and "on the night of 12 August 1961, East German soldiers began erecting the Berlin Wall" (infobox "Berlin Crisis: 4 June 1961"); East Berlin was made the 15th Bezirk in 1961.
wars.note: A crisis, not a war; listed so the reviewer can see it was considered. No contested zone: the sector boundary stayed where it was.

certainty.note: The GDR's whole outline was fixed: the Oder-Neisse line to Poland (Potsdam 1945, recognised by the GDR in the 1950 Treaty of Zgorzelec and again by the 1990 German-Polish Border Treaty), the Czech frontier, the Baltic coast, and the inner German border of 1,381 km, fortified from 1952. The Baltic sea border with Poland was defined by a treaty of 1989 (Oder-Neisse page).

notes: Four pages opened (budget up to 5). The GDR changed no outer border in its life; its five Cliopatria shapes differ by under 0.7 % (the 1973-75 shape is +693 km2 with no dated cause: treated as noise). The ledger is therefore short: birth, accession, absorption, dissolution. Non-territorial events the pages date and a viewer may want as captions: the Treaty of Zgorzelec with Poland in 1950 (the Oder-Neisse page gives the year only; it recognises, does not move, the line), the 1952 replacement of the five states by districts, the Soviet grant of "full sovereignty" on 20 September 1955 (East Germany page; the Western Allies did not recognise it), the Berlin Wall of 12/13 August 1961, the opening of the border on 9 November 1989, the currency union of 1 July 1990 and the Two Plus Four treaty of 12 September 1990. Level-of-control (rule 4): the Soviet zone of 1945-49 is the allied-occupied-germany dossier's; this dossier does not draw the GDR as a Soviet client because the pages do not use that word; the USSR dossier (eu-17) may. Counterpart "allied-occupied-germany" and "federated-republic-of-germany" are other writers' dossiers (both exist in polities/ on 2026-11-01). Gazetteer: all names resolve as written (German admin1 spellings Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thüringen).
